found.title: File:Old schoolroom, Pen-ffynnon - geograph.org.uk - 942366.jpg
found.credit: From geograph.org.uk
found.desc: Old schoolroom, Pen-ffynnon. A mock-up of an old school at the Museum of Childhood. The desks came from the original school nearby at Cenarth. On the desks in the foreground are slates and a ink-can for filling the ink wells, behind them a cane and a wooden device for forcing children to sit up straight, to the right a Welsh-not, a piece of wood that would be passed on, from child to child, to anyone who failed to speak in English.

found.title: File:"Y Welsh Note". Trysorfa y Plant.png
found.credit: Johnes, Martin (2024) Welsh Not (p. 273)
found.desc: Y Welsh Note (The Welsh Note), an illustration depicting the Welsh Not in an 1879 addition of a Welsh language children's magazine Trysorfa y Plant. The Welsh Not was used in some 19th-century schools in Wales to punish children for speaking Welsh. The Welsh Note was an alternative name for the practice.

found.title: File:Extract from the 1877 logbook of Llanddoged school.png
found.credit: Johnes, Martin (2024) Welsh Not (p. 280)
found.desc: The logbook reads; 22 August 1877 - Some of the parents complained of their children being allowed to speak Welsh, I cautioned the children, and made use of the (Welsh Stick). 24th - Attendance fair this day. Introduced a new song this afternoon (addewidion mawl a gwerthfawr.) 27th - Mr Rich a [Richard?] Passy attendance officer for the Llanewrst School Board District visited, no. present 22 boys and 23 girls total 45. Singing (Knocking, knocking; who is there;) 30th - Holiday, annual agricultural show held at Llanwrst 3rd Sept - Few extra lessons given this day at 1.30 to the second standard

found.title: File:Taflen Robat Griffiths, Prifysgol Bangor Gorff 2025 - Early pamphlet written by Owain Owain as part of Tafod y Ddraig July 2025.jpg
found.credit: Own work
found.desc: Early pamphlet written by Owain Owain as part of Tafod y Ddraig(Welsh Language Society) on 20 July 1964, commemorating student Robat Gruffudd refusing his degree in Prifysgol Bangor because the university refuses to use the Welsh language. This weas one of the first Welsh Language Society's protests; it was organised by Owain Owain (Owen Owen). All of Owain Owain's literature has been passed on to his son Robin Owain (Llywelyn2000), the uploader.
